heartbeat.title: Consequence framing beats the dynamic baseline
heartbeat.body_html: Our Winback test showed that consequence framing, spelling out what a subscriber stands to lose, drove stronger opens and revenue against the Retentics dynamic baseline. The transferable lesson is that lapsing customers respond to a concrete stake rather than a gentle nudge, and this framing is now banked permanently in your Winback sequence. Two other tests held their controls this month, which costs nothing and tells us exactly where the current messaging is already strong. That asymmetry is the point: winners stay, losers leave no trace, and the program keeps compounding.

narrative.html: Flows delivered $75,017 and held 29.9% of total store revenue, up slightly from June and well above the 12% pre-takeover baseline. This is the contribution that runs automatically, independent of the month's promotional push.

Flow revenue per email delivered rose to $0.461 from $0.451, and each flow email now earns 9.8x what a campaign email earns ($0.461 vs $0.047). The automated layer is doing the heavy lifting per send.
Flows accounted for 68% of email revenue this month. Deliverability stayed clean, with unsubscribes at 0.315% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.009%, both comfortably in healthy territory.

Total flow revenue eased 5.6% versus June, in line with the wider store's demand for the month. On the campaign side, 9 sends went out at a $0.047 RPR; campaigns are your team's to run, but if you'd ever like a fresh set of eyes on them we're happy to take a look.

monthly.title_sub: Flows earned $75,017 in July and held nearly 30% of total store revenue, close to double the pre-takeover rate.
